items.evidence: The 26.1.2 tree inherits the 26.1.1 tree's re-ported 26.3-form oracle sources wholesale (the 26.1.1->26.1.2 delta touches no oracle file — verified by diff -rq over the parity dirs: no output), so the same 17 files fail identically here with identical error counts: 9 newly failing vs 26.1 (VanillaBasicFeatureOracle 2 errors, VanillaBiomePlacementOracle 8, VanillaBlockTransformerOracle 3, VanillaBrewingFuelOracle 8, VanillaFeaturePlacementOracle 3, VanillaFeatureSortOracle 1, VanillaFillLayerOracle 1, VanillaReplaceBlockOracle 1, VanillaScatteredOreOracle 1), 7 with error-count growth vs 26.1 (VanillaBrewingOracle cascade -> 14 own errors, VanillaDecorationRegionOracle 5 -> 6, VanillaFeatureCatalogOracle 5 -> 11, VanillaFeatureGraphOracle 3 -> 4, VanillaFeatureRegionOracle 7 -> 10, VanillaFirstPersonOracle 11 -> 20, VanillaTreeFeatureOracle 8 -> 11), and 1 new file vs 26.1 (VanillaSteppedInterpolationOracle, 16 errors, replacing the passing VanillaInterpolationOracle). No file fails new or worse vs 26.1.1 — the full-field diff of the measured table against 26.1.1's is ZERO deviations across all 391 files, because the 26.1.1->26.1.2 jar delta changes no public API (class-bytes diff: 8 changed class files, 5 top-level classes; the only member-level change is two private Checkbox members, ROWS and overflowsRowLimit, invisible to oracles). The re-port signature is the 26.3 unconfigured-Feature form: Feature.DIRECT_CODEC (absent from 26.1.2; only ConfiguredFeature.DIRECT_CODEC exists, javap-verified), no-arg new Feature() (26.1.2's Feature takes only Codec<FC>), the 4-arg place(WorldGenLevel,ChunkGenerator,RandomSource,BlockPos) (26.1.2's abstract place takes FeaturePlaceContext), FeaturePlacer-based placement, plus the 26.3-only BrewingFuel component (0 jar entries), BlockTransformer component, BrewingInput/BrewingRecipe/PotionIngredient/RecipePropertySet crafting APIs, PositionAndRotation (0 jar entries) and LivingEntity.SwingState (0 jar entries; FirstPersonOracle also uses the 26.3 boolean swing(InteractionHand,SwingAnimation,boolean) — 26.1.2's LivingEntity has only swing(InteractionHand) and swing(InteractionHand,boolean)). The 26.1-adapted forms are the repair template for all 17 (e.g. VanillaBrewingFuelOracle's 26.1 version documents '26.1 has no brewing_fuel component: fuel is any item in the tag, 20 uses, flat 400 ticks'). One re-ported file still compiles (VanillaSimpleBlockOracle, CONFIGURED_FEATURE -> FEATURE registry). No repair attempted in this batch (measurement + triage only).

systemic_note: Same root cause as the pilot's G1/G3/G5/G6, two versions further back: the 26.1.2 tree carries 26.3 API forms (packages, constructors, abstract methods, holder classes) for things that do not exist in vanilla 26.1.2, and every such reference fails loudly at javac time in the oracles (unlike the port code, where the same pattern silently degrades). The 26.1.2 run adds no new breakage: the measured table is identical to 26.1.1's in every field (zero deviations across all 391 files), because the oracle sources are byte-identical between the trees and the 26.1.1->26.1.2 jar delta changes no public API (the only member-level change is two private Checkbox members). The re-ported oracle sources (O9, 17 files) are inherited unchanged from 26.1.1, as is the +10 regression vs 26.1 they carry. The EntityTypes holder move (O5, 31 files) still dominates the inherited breakage: 26.1.2 predates it, so every EntityTypes.X reference fails; the translation back to EntityType.X is mechanical and javap-verified. Two mechanical groups (LocalPlayer ctor, 20 files with 7 single-cause; Level.fuelValues(), 4 files) rescue files with two signature translations. The densityfunction (O4, 17 files) and renderpearl/material.rule (O6) groups are the genuinely hard ones: 26.3-only APIs with no 26.1.2 equivalent to translate to import-by-import. Compiling is not running (O8) — the runtime layer is unmeasured and each oracle needs an end-to-end driver run.
